currentStage: Milestone 12 is complete with accepted typography, elevation, Aqua Core Icon integration, semantic state motion, and all twenty-two shared component primitives. The independent aqua-components crate owns renderer-neutral anatomy, stable state geometry, input activation, and accessibility semantics. Settings Audio supplies the final real slider consumer through a bounded persistent 0-100 output-volume preference and mute state without claiming physical hardware support. Its UI now exposes unavailable, starting, degraded, applying, and applied states, keeps the last authoritative value visible while a desired change is pending, and enables slider/mute input only after authoritative acknowledgement. ADR 0004 selects ALSA/eudev, per-user PipeWire, WirePlumber policy, and an authoritative Aqua adapter for the R4 audio path. The OS baseline is pinned to Buildroot 2025.02.17 LTS. The graphical path runs as locked aqua UID/GID 1000 with private /run/user/1000 and explicit video, audio, and input groups while recovery remains separate. Its packaged media supervisor proves finite ordered lifecycle and degraded state. The renderer-independent aqua-service-adapters crate proves bounded typed device and route state, monotonic reconciliation, retained desired volume and mute across service loss, and acknowledgement-gated backend application. Its typed transport has an opt-in WirePlumber 0.5 native binding with a versioned fixed-size ABI, finite synchronization waits, strict Rust validation, mixer controls, and configured-default-output calls without command parsing. The separate Buildroot audio profile applies an audio-only overlay and Intel HDA plus ACPI PCI hotplug kernel fragment after the disabled base profile, records exact stack versions, enables only the per-user supervisor, and passes a fail-closed contract against the complete final rootfs artifact. Declared Intel HDA QEMU evidence proves sink/source-node discovery, volume/mute, 48 kHz stereo S16LE output into a non-silent WAV capture, bounded WirePlumber restart recovery, a controlled 4,800-frame zero-PCM input stream, and a separate deterministic 4,800-frame non-silent D-Bus-injected input stream without host microphone access. A bounded D-Bus input failure additionally proves one-polarity buffered data is rejected rather than reported as valid bipolar capture while the media graph and recovery shell remain responsive. Active playback now also proves PipeWire loss produces an explicit 480-frame Broken pipe interruption without false completion, followed by ordered service recovery and a new non-silent 48,000-frame playback. Active WirePlumber loss now proves the same client fails explicitly, the supervisor retires both old media processes, attempt 2/restart 1 restores the ordered pair, and a new 48,000-frame playback is non-silent. Repeated real PipeWire loss now proves the three-restart budget degrades after attempt four, cleans up both services and the PipeWire socket, blocks new playback, and preserves recovery-shell access. Native controls now independently prove one healthy acknowledgement before the same four PipeWire losses and reject control open without false acknowledgement after the cleaned degraded state. Their WirePlumber counterpart proves the same healthy precondition, three complete media-pair renewals, and fail-closed control rejection after the fourth policy loss reaches `failed_service=wireplumber` degradation. Repeated real WirePlumber loss now independently proves three complete pair renewals followed by failed_service=wireplumber degradation on attempt four, full process/socket cleanup, blocked playback, and preserved recovery-shell access. Controlled capture restart exhaustion now proves an exact 4,800-frame zero-PCM precondition before four PipeWire losses and rejects a new capture without false success after the cleaned degraded state, without host-microphone access. Its WirePlumber counterpart proves the same precondition, three complete media-pair renewals, `failed_service=wireplumber` degradation on the fourth loss, and fail-closed capture rejection without host-microphone access. Active controlled capture now proves PipeWire loss after 480 zero-PCM frames produces an explicit Broken pipe interruption without false completion, followed by ordered recovery and a new exact 4,800-frame capture without host-microphone access. Active controlled capture during WirePlumber loss now proves the client fails explicitly, both old media processes retire before attempt 2/restart 1 restores the ordered pair, and a new exact 4,800-frame zero-PCM capture completes without host-microphone access. Active virtual input-device removal now proves native topology reports input-route-loss after 480 injected frames, exposes zero remaining inputs, blocks new capture without false completion, and leaves media services plus recovery responsive without host microphone access. Native volume/mute controls now also prove an unavailable PipeWire graph rejects acknowledgement at bridge open and accepts a new control cycle only after ordered recovery restores a different PipeWire process. The WirePlumber policy-loss counterpart proves the resulting full-stack outage rejects acknowledgement, both old media processes retire, and controls succeed again only on the replacement attempt 2/restart 1 graph. A two-controller output profile also proves two authoritative sinks, native configured-default switching, effective-route acknowledgement, and non-silent playback on both independent WAV backends. A selected-output removal profile requires QMP deletion acknowledgement, one-device ALSA and authoritative native topology, and non-silent fallback playback. A replug-boundary profile requires QEMU's runtime HDA codec rejection, rolls back the incomplete replacement controller through acknowledged deletion, rejects false restoration, and proves a second non-silent playback on the stable fallback. A complementary non-default removal profile proves PCI 04.0 remains authoritative while PCI 05.0 is removed, the topology converges to one output, and non-silent playback stays on the same route before and after removal. Its active-stream profile removes 05.0 after 480 frames and requires the same default-route client to complete 48,000 frames without interruption or hidden recovery. The selected-route active counterpart removes authoritative PCI 05.0 after 480 frames, detects route loss through native topology rather than buffered PCM write success, forbids false completion, and requires a new client to complete 48,000 non-silent frames on fallback PCI 04.0. The packaged production adapter probe now proves the native graph generation remains stable across three rejected control submissions, blocks the fourth call before it reaches the bridge, and reopens submission only after a real graph change advances the generation through final authoritative acknowledgement. A separate selected-route control-loss profile binds the pending volume request to PCI 05.0, removes that output while fallback PCI 04.0 already has the desired value, and proves the coincidence cannot acknowledge the removed target: the old request is rejected or lost and no redundant submission is needed. Its mute counterpart prepares fallback 04.0 muted, binds pending mute to unmuted selected 05.0, and proves the same lost-request behavior when 05.0 disappears. The default image remains sound-free and disabled. Packaged Bochs DRM QEMU now proves the R2 production GBM/KMS path for all four workloads with direct dma-buf scanout, zero production readbacks and CPU copies, and isolated diagnostic readback. Three independent packaged boots produced 12 passing workload records and three isolated diagnostics; the reviewed qemu-tcg-bochs-v1 profile now enforces fixed frame, input, CPU, memory, and zero-drop regression limits while explicitly leaving the physical budget unselected. The initial five-minute R2 QEMU soak proves one long-lived compositor process with Files and Settings, periodic real input, bounded timing and resource growth, zero crashes, clean recovery return, and isolated diagnostic readback. A repeated acknowledgement-gated qualification review now proves three independent cold-boot production GBM/KMS runs with three isolated diagnostic records, 213 presented frames, minimum 1,319,699 ms observation, minimum 38 input samples, minimum 94 keyboard events, bounded timing and resources, full cleanup, and recovery return while retaining physical_evidence=false and release_ready=false. Positive output replug, physical presentation budgets, and other media error behavior remain open. Physical MSI Sword 17 validation remains unauthorized until read-only evidence is reviewed.

readiness.summary: The booted Buildroot image and custom compositor have substantial packaged-QEMU evidence, but the mandatory R1-R7 product gates remain open. Roadmap progress is not a release-readiness score.

rules: Roadmap implementation progress is the rounded arithmetic mean of the 13 M0-M12 phase percentages so the public value is reproducible.
The roadmap percentage measures scoped implementation work; it is not a daily-use, hardware-support, or release-readiness score.
Aqua Linux v1.0 readiness is governed separately by the mandatory gates in docs/aqua-linux/v1-readiness.md.
Progress advances only when bootable OS, compositor, installer, or validation contracts move forward.
Host mockups and website work do not count as OS completion unless they become packaged runtime assets.
The project remains Buildroot-based and does not use Ubuntu, Debian, KDE, GNOME, XFCE, LXQt, or a theme-pack base.

phases.name: Repository and Build Skeleton
phases.summary: Rust workspace, Buildroot external tree, scripts, docs, assets folder, and local checks exist.

phases.name: Buildroot Boot to Text Recovery
phases.summary: QEMU x86_64 boots a minimal Buildroot image to BusyBox recovery shell with serial boot markers.

phases.name: Asset and Visual System Intake
phases.summary: Public contracts capture the permanent desktop, application, search, first-party app, installer, completion, and four-theme direction derived from private Git-ignored boards. Approved transparent brand exports and the reproducible pale-wave wallpaper are used by the runtime. Thirteen project-authored Aqua Core Icons permanently cover core application, desktop, notification, and status roles with explicit MIT licensing; no temporary icon package remains.

phases.name: Nested Aqua Compositor Prototype
phases.summary: Smithay/calloop, host preview, recovery-safe output, and QEMU DRM/KMS integration are complete for the prototype milestone. The packaged supervisor limits rapid failures and returns to recovery after budget exhaustion; QEMU proves three real compositor failures and two bounded restarts. The boot gate requires aqua.boot_graphics=1 plus a separate graphics profile, tracks PID/state, rejects duplicates, stays disabled by default, and starts the real DRM-Wayland compositor from rcS when explicitly enabled while preserving recovery TTY access.

phases.name: Scene and Surface Renderer
phases.summary: The Smithay GLES2 renderer composes the packaged wallpaper, shared surfaces, optional two-pass blur, and live wl_shm textures at the native output size. Physical DRM retains XRGB8888 GBM front/back dma-buf scanout. The packaged kernel now enables Bochs DRM and the default R2 QEMU target proves the production GBM/KMS path at 1280x800 with direct dma-buf scanout, zero production full-frame readbacks and CPU copies across idle, shell interaction, animation, and Files plus Settings workloads, followed by an isolated diagnostic readback. Its acknowledgement-gated qualification profile now has three independent cold-boot runs with three isolated diagnostics, 213 presented frames, minimum 1,319,699 ms observation, minimum 38 input samples, minimum 94 keyboard events, zero crashes or drops, bounded timing and resource growth, full cleanup, and recovery return. Virtio remains the explicit legacy CPU-copy fallback; physical evidence and release readiness remain separate gates.

phases.name: Basic Wayland Client Support
phases.summary: The packaged QEMU DRM session runs the upstream Weston simple-shm C reference client as an independent compatibility fixture beside an Aqua state client. Aqua's compositor exposes the xdg-shell and wl_shm protocol path, composites their 250x250 and 384x256 buffers, returns frame callbacks, records damage, changes focus and stacking, handles move, resize, size constraints, maximize/restore, fullscreen/restore, repeated configure acknowledgements, compositor close, stale-focus cleanup, surviving-window repaint, final empty-desktop repaint, and recovery return. The Weston compositor, shells, backends, and desktop session are neither packaged nor started.

phases.name: Boot Aqua Compositor in QEMU
phases.summary: The packaged compositor boots through the explicit aqua.boot_graphics=1 gate while default boot remains text recovery. In one aqua-compositor process, real Smithay compositor, shm, xdg-shell, and Aqua Seat globals bind /run/aqua/aqua-wayland-drm-0, dispatch clients and DRM page flips, and discover real virtio input through libinput/udev. The supervised boot profile now remains active until controlled stop or fatal error. QEMU verifies two complete start-stop cycles, socket and PID cleanup, client termination, CRTC restoration, GBM release, and recovery return.

phases.name: First-Party Shell Surfaces
phases.summary: The state-driven shell starts packaged Aqua Files and Aqua Settings through strict executable preflight and reusable process supervision. Production QEMU maps and raises first-party windows by XDG app_id, tracks damage, closes applications, reaps failures, and removes stale surfaces. Notifications, real system overview, desktop icon interactions, target-aware Properties, confined Trash, and the confirmed session menu are integrated. Applications and Global Search are separate centered modes with scaled pointer targets and real quick actions. The bottom shell separates these controls from the centered app dock and three real workspaces; keyboard and pointer paths activate workspaces, and focused windows can move between them.

phases.name: Terminal App
phases.summary: A packaged aqua-terminal opens as a supervised aqua.terminal xdg-toplevel with Aqua chrome and a dark readable scrim. It uses portable-pty for a real /bin/sh session and vt100 for mature terminal parsing, renders the prompt, coalesces PTY output into bounded redraws, and resizes both the PTY and parser grid. Aqua boot mounts devpts and provides /dev/ptmx. QEMU forwards all 40 press/release events for 'echo aquaterminalok', observes Enter, parses output, applies Alt+F8 resize through a real xdg configure to a 640x478 buffer and 74x21 grid, resizes the PTY, repaints, captures the window, closes with Alt+F4, reaps the process, and confirms restart=never. Pointer titlebar and bottom-right resize requests are implemented; broader key and clipboard support remain later enhancements.

phases.name: Graphical Installer MVP
phases.summary: The packaged installer executes and boots the complete separately gated installation, proves failure cleanup, and emits QEMU-validated transaction progress. Seven deterministic Rust-rendered setup screens feed a packaged aqua.installer wl_shm xdg-toplevel client; QEMU proves full-output composition and navigation from Welcome through Completed. An explicit presentation-only rehearsal consumes the canonical non-executing 20-step graph, renders progress at 40%, 65%, and 95%, reaches Completed at 100%, emits seven distinct screendumps, and proves transaction_executed=false. Real virtio pointer input activates the Welcome footer and selects a Language row through renderer-shared geometry before keyboard navigation resumes. Summary real mode requires a shared target-bound destructive-acknowledgement checkbox before the unchanged exact uppercase ERASE phrase; target changes invalidate the acknowledgement. Full-output client focus takes precedence over hidden shell hit targets, modifier state reaches the focused Wayland client, blocked disks and hidden controls reject hits, and disk/profile application retains explicit activation.

phases.name: MSI Sword 17 Hardware Validation
phases.summary: Real hardware validation is intentionally later; QEMU remains the first reproducible target.

phases.name: Polish and Public Readiness
phases.summary: The v1 desktop and installer contracts are documented. The runtime has a compact top bar, reproducible pale-wave wallpaper, permanent Aqua Core Icons, separate Applications and Global Search surfaces, three bottom shell groups, shared first-party window chrome, four live-refreshed themes, and three real workspaces. Current QEMU captures carry a provenance manifest, the public hardware matrix prevents physical support overclaims, and the default-image gate enforces recovery-safe startup. Structured issue forms, private security routing, canonical labels, a pull request safety checklist, and CI-enforced contributor contracts now define public intake and triage.

phases.name: Visual Fidelity and Component System
phases.summary: The shared aqua-text crate, tokenized elevation path, Aqua Core Icon pipeline, and semantic motion system have deterministic host fixtures plus packaged QEMU evidence. The independent aqua-components crate owns renderer-neutral anatomy, stable state geometry, input activation, and accessibility semantics for all 22 catalog entries. Settings Audio supplies the final real slider consumer through a bounded persistent 0-100 output-volume preference, mute state, exact renderer/input geometry, and fail-closed authoritative adapter availability. Desired state persists, while displayed service state and backend application require reconciliation. Explicit unavailable, starting, degraded, applying, and applied UI states keep pending desired values separate from the last authoritative value and disable slider/mute input until acknowledgement. The typed transport has an opt-in bounded native WirePlumber binding and a validated audio-only rootfs contract. Declared Intel HDA QEMU acceptance proves output playback, sink/source-node discovery, volume/mute, service restart recovery, controlled zero-PCM input, deterministic non-silent D-Bus-injected input without host microphone access, rejection of a bounded D-Bus input failure without false capture success or recovery-shell loss, explicit active-playback interruption plus ordered recovery after nextSteps: After authorized hardware inventory and bring-up, select a separate physical-target presentation budget without treating the three independent QEMU TCG qualification runs as responsiveness evidence.
Implement the first R3 clipboard and primary-selection ownership boundary with independent-client tests, without weakening privileged protocol policy.
Implement the R3-R6 Wayland compatibility, unprivileged session, system service, accessibility, internationalization, signed update, rollback, and security gates.

After core desktop functionality supplies real consumers, consolidate the proven typography, component, layout, focus, accessibility, lifecycle, and renderer contracts into the internal Aqua UI framework defined by ADR 0003.
Collect and review a sanitized read-only inventory from the MSI Sword 17 before authorizing any physical boot or installation validation.
